name: Maryland

regulator.name: Maryland Department of Labor, Athlete Agents Licensing Program

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract includes endorsement contracts, so NIL deals are covered (Bus. Reg. 4-401). Anyone who connects an athlete with another agent also counts as an agent.
summary: Get a license from the Department of Labor. $25 to apply, then $1,000 when approved. Good for 2 years.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent license application
Mail it to the Athlete Agents Licensing Program
steps.detail: 1100 N. Eutaw St., Room 121, Baltimore, MD 21201.

steps.text: Pay the $1,000 license invoice when approved
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, plus any other pay you get for the deal. Anyone not on your license application who gets paid, expenses the athlete pays back, your services, how long it lasts and the date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student-athlete box next to the athlete's signature
steps.detail: Bold capital letters. Use the exact words from Maryland law.

steps.text: Tell the athlete before they sign that it may cost them their eligibility
steps.detail: Skipping this is against the law.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Notify the athletic director within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Do it in writing, or before the athlete's next scheduled game if that comes first. The athlete must tell them too.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days if they want
steps.detail: They cancel by telling you in writing. They owe you nothing and keep anything you gave them. This right can't be waived.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law (SPARTA) bans pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses, every contract and your recruiting costs. The state can inspect them during business hours.

steps.text: Never give false info or gifts to get an athlete to sign
steps.detail: Don't give anything of value to the athlete before they sign, or to anyone but the athlete or another licensed agent. Breaking these rules is a crime, with a fine up to $10,000 and up to 1 year in jail.
$1,000. The license runs 2 years from the day it was issued.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The Labor Department site lists no phone number. Use its contact page at https://labor.maryland.gov/contactinfo/ to confirm how to reach the program.
The $25 application fee comes from the Labor Department site, not the statute. The statute sets only the $1,000 license and renewal fees (Bus. Reg. 4-405).
